topic: The Physics of Refraction: A Proof of Snell's Law
target_audience: University Physics Students / Advanced High School Physics Students

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Life Guard' Problem
lecture_lines: Lifeguards must reach drowning swimmers quickly.
Running on sand is slower than swimming.
A straight path is not always fastest.
We seek the path of least time.
[Asset: LifeguardPathAnimation] Angle impacts total travel time.
animations: 1. Display a beach [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/beach.svg] (#F0E68C) and ocean [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ocean.svg] (#4682B4) boundary.
2. Show a lifeguard [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lifeguard.svg] on beach and swimmer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/swimmer.svg] in ocean.
3. Introduce the lifeguard's [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lifeguard.svg] need to find shortest time.
4. Highlight path choice from beach to ocean boundary.
5. Emphasize the intersection point changing with path using a swimmer [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/swimmer.svg] icon.

sections.title: Prerequisite Geometry: Defining the Interface
lecture_lines: Consider two media with different indices.
They are separated by a flat boundary.
[Asset: InterfaceGeometryAnimation] Measure angles relative to the normal.
animations: 1. Draw a line representing the boundary interface.
2. Label the normal line perpendicular to the interface using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg].
3. Identify incident angle theta_1 and refractive angle theta_2 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fiber.svg].

sections.title: Mathematical Formulation of Time
lecture_lines: Total time depends on distance and speed.
Speed relates to the index of refraction.
[Asset: TimeEquationAnimation] Express total time using boundary distance x.
animations: 3. Relate distance to geometric trigonometric functions [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg].

sections.title: Deriving Snell’s Law via Fermat's Principle
lecture_lines: Apply Fermat’s Principle: minimize total time.
[Asset: SnellDerivationAnimation] Result: n1 sin theta1 = n2 sin theta2.
This confirms the law of refraction.
animations: 1. Differentiate T with respect to position variable x, while showing the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg].
2. Set dT/dx = 0 to find the minimum.
3. Rearrange terms to yield sin(theta_1)/v1 = sin(theta_2)/v2.
5. Flash the equation to emphasize Snell's Law result as the light ray passes through the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg].

sections.title: Conclusion: Real-world Synthesis
lecture_lines: Refraction follows the path of least time.
The lifeguard analogy holds true for light.
[Asset: RealWorldSynthesisAnimation] Nature optimizes to find efficiency.
animations: 1. Recap the lifeguard's path as a light ray using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lifeguard.svg].
2. Connect the geometric result to physical optics.
3. Conclude by showing Snell's Law governing nature with the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lifeguard.svg].
